_doc: Per-part settings keyed by part name (source of truth, set by whoever designs the part). _defaults apply to every part without its own entry; there is no default material (a printed part without one reports material null). process (print setup, resolved by checks/process.py): printer (printers.json), material (materials.json), nozzle_mm (default: the material's recommended nozzle), layer_height_mm and line_width_mm (default: the printer's values for that nozzle), up (manifest-frame direction away from the bed = layer normal, '+x' ... or a vector), plate_yaw_deg (turn about up on the plate, default 0), material_alternatives (other materials the part may be printed in), printed (overrides the role rule), seeded / seeded_keys (values derived from old free text, FEM axes or a bed-contact estimate, not yet confirmed: delete them when the designer confirms), layer_normal_axes (axes studied in the FEM runs; null = not set). expected_hardware: counts the checks compare with what the manifest contains. covers (shell parts): parts the shell covers, the vertical axis (x, y) the inner wall faces, and the lowest z of the inner wall that is measured. exact_fit.min_solid_mm3: only the STEP solids of at least this volume take part in the exact fit (a servo's housing without its internal gears). loadpath_slices: {axis, range_mm, n_slices} of the part's load-bearing span for the slab-area / severed-branch measurement (null = not set; values of the four R arm connectors are the arm study's STAGE_SLICE_SPECS). fem: per-part FEM setup (format in checks/fem_core.py); migrated from the old per-study scripts. geometry_thresholds: {sliver_mm2, micro_edge_mm, acute_normal_deg, g1_kink_deg}, what the geometry check counts as an event (smaller planar face, shorter planar edge with a bend over 10 deg, edge normal angle above, cylinder/plane kink up to); defaults = the old leg values, a part's own entry changes only the keys it names. loadpath_slices source: where set_by says so, axis and range are the dominant-axis span between the centroid of the part's FEM support holes and of its FEM load holes (checks/fem_core.holes_near), a first reading to be confirmed by the designer.

fem._doc: Leg stage 3 foot monocoque (leg fem_evaluate stage3_foot_monocoque; not in fem_refit). Supports: the foot-roll servo case's front / rear bolts; load: the sole pads at toe and heel. Link shifted: manifest frame = old r1 frame + 4 mm in x.
fem.open_difference: Re-run on the manifest roll-flip df7d03a5e2610e97, loose load kept: the load is the sole / sensor pocket pad contact, not a metal case or horn, so no rigid patch (the support is the foot-roll case screws, fixed). Stored h is now 3.0 (the finest level under the 6 GB cap on the roll-flip STEP; h 2.2 peaks above 6.18 GB with CG + AMG). Recovery PAHT-CF z at h 3.0: p99 2.08 / peak 12.6 / displacement 0.33 mm (ratio 42), reaction + wrench 0.0 %. fem_setup: supports 373.7 / 380.5 mm2, load 3719 mm2, 0 shared nodes. Earlier notes: The old stage-3 numbers (old pipeline mesh h 3.0, r1 frame) are history, not reproduced. Solver and patch port are exact: on the old pipeline's own h 3.0 mesh (42731 nodes) this module's legacy patches give identical patch weights (main 1258 / idler 841 / load 8114 nodes) and, through fem_core.solve, p99 2.145 / peak 10.57 / disp 0.1139 vs the old pipeline 2.134 / 11.59 / 0.1136 (+0.5 / -9 / +0.3 %). gmsh meshes the part differently in the manifest frame (41931 nodes at h 3.0, main support 1076 nodes), which moves p99 +37 % and displacement +61..+72 % at h 3.0: the foot is sensitive to meshing at that size. The stored setup runs at h 2.2 (85649 nodes, CG + AMG: 143 s, peak 4.7 GB; spsolve exceeded the 6 GB cap). h 2.2, PAHT dry, recovery, z, p99 / peak / disp: legacy_coordinates 3.061 / 18.12 / 0.196, stored 2.879 / 14.31 / 0.186 (-6 / -21 / -5 %). Mesh-frame spread of p99 for the same legacy patches: 2.13 (old mesh h 3.0), ~2.93 (manifest frame h 3.0), 3.06 (h 2.2). Stored patches: load = contact with the sensor pocket pad (2689 mm2 vs old sole box 2387), supports = contact with the foot-roll case screws (373 / 382 mm2 vs old 524 / 320). Variants mesh_h3p0 / legacy_coordinates_h3p0 keep the h 3.0 comparison.

convergence.stored_h_result: NOT converged, only one level fits: h 3.0 runs (64242 nodes, CG + AMG, peak 3.80 GB); h 2.6 fails in gmsh (empty tet list, also on the clean() STEP); h 2.2 (120390 nodes) is stopped by memguard at 6.18 GB even with the CG path (cap not raised). Stored h 3.0 = the finest level that fits. Earlier on the proof STEP (4e883237, 85649 nodes) h 3.0 vs 2.2 differed by about 4 % p99.
